label: Access this window
summary: A game function of the call-ally window that hands back the window itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Its return type is listed as unregistered, and vanilla never uses it with this window. Going by its name, it gives the window object to another function.

label: Can send offer
summary: Whether the offer to call the ally into a war can be sent right now.
details: Vanilla puts it in the `enabled` line of the send offer button of the call-ally window, so the button works only when this is true. The game does not say what makes it true.

label: Close window
summary: Closes the call-ally window.
details: Vanilla runs it from an `onclick` line of the call-ally interaction window. It returns nothing.

label: Call ally description
summary: The descriptive text shown in the call-ally window.
details: Going by its name and its use, vanilla shows it as the `text` of a text box in the call-ally interaction window.

label: Confirmation window
summary: The general interaction confirmation window data that the call-ally window uses as its data context.
details: Vanilla sets it as the `datacontext` of the call-ally window itself, and the send button inside reads `CharacterInteractionConfirmationWindow.GetSendName`, so the window reuses the general confirmation window's data. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: Send offer tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the send offer button in the call-ally window.
details: Vanilla puts it in the `tooltip` line of that button (`send_offer_button`). The game does not say what the text contains.

label: War list items
summary: The list of wars shown in the call-ally window, one entry per war.
details: Going by its name and its use, vanilla uses it as the `datamodel` of a list in the call-ally interaction window; each entry is a war item of that window. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: Has wars
summary: Whether the call-ally window has any wars to list.
details: Vanilla uses it as `Not(CallAllyInteractionWindow.HasWars)` in the `visible` line of the empty-list message, whose text says there are no wars to select. (The input missed this use because it is written without a space.)

label: This window
summary: A game function of the call-ally window that stands for the window itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla does not use it with this window. Its return type is listed as unregistered. The same name is used with other types to pass an object along.

label: Send offer
summary: Sends the offer to call the ally into a war.
details: Vanilla runs it from the `onclick` of the send offer button in the call-ally window. It returns nothing.

label: Access this war item
summary: A game function of a war entry in the call-ally window that hands back the entry itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Its return type is listed as unregistered, and vanilla never uses it with this type.

label: War item tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of a war entry in the call-ally window.
details: Going by its name and its use, vanilla puts it in the `tooltip` line of the call-ally interaction window.

label: The war
summary: The war that a war entry in the call-ally window stands for.
details: Going by its name and its use, vanilla sets it as the `datacontext` of a widget in the call-ally window, so that widget can show the war's own data. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: Is enabled
summary: Whether a war entry in the call-ally window can be used.
details: Going by its name and its use, vanilla puts it in an `enabled` line of the call-ally interaction window.

label: Is selected
summary: Whether a war entry in the call-ally window is the selected one.
details: Going by its name and its use, vanilla puts it in a `down` line (the pressed look of a button) of the call-ally interaction window.

label: On click
summary: Reacts to a click on a war entry in the call-ally window.
details: Vanilla runs it from an `onclick` line of the call-ally interaction window. Going by the name and the use of the selected check, it selects that war. It returns nothing.

label: This war item
summary: A game function of a war entry in the call-ally window that stands for the entry itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla does not use it with this type. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: Access this camera
summary: Hands the camera itself to another function.
details: Vanilla passes it in the court scene editor window to the functions that make a camera active, edit its description, or make it the default one. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: This camera
summary: The camera itself, used as an argument for other functions.
details: Vanilla passes it in the court scene editor window to functions that ask whether a camera is active, toggle whether it is expanded, or check if it is expanded. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: Access this camera item
summary: A game function of a camera entry that hands back the entry itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Its return type is listed as unregistered, and vanilla never uses it with this type.

label: Activate camera
summary: Switches the view to this camera.
details: Vanilla runs it from an `onclick` line in the royal court screenshot window. Going by its name, it makes this camera the active one. It returns nothing.

label: Camera name
summary: The name of the camera, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as the `text` of labels in the royal court screenshot window.

label: Is selected
summary: Whether this camera is the selected one.
details: Vanilla uses it in the royal court screenshot window to choose a button frame: `BoolTo1And2` turns the answer into frame 1 or 2.

label: This camera item
summary: A game function of a camera entry that stands for the entry itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla does not use it with this type. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: Access this vassal entry
summary: A game function of a vassal entry in the factions window that hands back the entry itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Its return type is listed as unregistered, and vanilla never uses it with this type.

label: Blocked vassal tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for a vassal who cannot create or join a faction.
details: Going by its name and its use, vanilla puts it in the `tooltip` line of the factions window. The game does not say what the text contains.

label: The vassal
summary: The vassal character of this entry (going by the type's name, one who cannot create or join a faction).
details: Returns a character. Vanilla sets it as the `datacontext` of a widget in the factions window, so the widget can show that character's data.

label: Is soft block
summary: Whether the block on creating or joining a faction is a soft one.
details: Vanilla uses it in a `visible` line of the factions window, so something is shown only for soft blocks. The game does not say what makes a block soft.

label: This vassal entry
summary: A game function of a vassal entry in the factions window that stands for the entry itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla does not use it with this type. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: Access this capital icon
summary: A game function of a capital icon on the map that hands back the icon itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Its return type is listed as unregistered, and vanilla never uses it with this type.

label: Capital owner
summary: The character who owns the capital that the map icon shows.
details: Returns a character. Vanilla uses it as a `datacontext` in the map icon layer, and also checks `GetOwner.IsPlayer` to show something only for player-owned capitals.

label: Capital province
summary: The province that the capital map icon sits in.
details: Returns a province. Vanilla does not use it with this type; going by its name only. Other types use a function of the same name the same way.

label: Capital title
summary: The title of the capital that the map icon shows.
details: Returns a title. Vanilla does not use it with this type; going by its name only.

label: Is at war with me
summary: Whether the capital's owner is at war with the player.
details: Vanilla uses it in `visible` lines of the map icon layer, where it shows an icon named `at_war_icon`. Going by its name, 'me' is the player and the check concerns the capital's owner.

label: Is land liege for landless
summary: A yes/no check on a capital map icon whose meaning the game does not document.
details: Going by its name only, it concerns a landless character and the land-holding liege. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Is land owner for landless
summary: A yes/no check on a capital map icon whose meaning the game does not document.
details: Going by its name only, it concerns a landless character and the owner of the land. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Is large
summary: Whether the capital map icon is the large kind; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Is liege
summary: A yes/no check on the capital's owner about a liege relation to the player; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name only. Whether it means the owner is the player's liege is a guess. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Is me
summary: A yes/no check whether the capital belongs to the player, going by its name.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Is my ally
summary: Whether the capital's owner is an ally of the player.
details: Vanilla uses it in `visible` lines of the map icon layer, where it shows an icon named `ally_war_icon`. Going by its name, 'my' is the player.

label: Is my ally in war
summary: Whether the capital's owner is an ally of the player who is currently in a war.
details: Vanilla uses it in a `visible` line of the map icon layer that shows an animated icon named `ally_war_anim`. The meaning (ally of the player who is in a war) rests on its name.

label: Is my ally not in war
summary: Whether the capital's owner is an ally of the player who is not in a war, going by its name.
details: Going by its name only, and as the opposite of the 'in war' check. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Is my raid target
summary: A yes/no check whether the capital's owner is a target of the player's raids, going by its name.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Is other realm
summary: A yes/no check whether the capital is in a realm other than the player's, going by its name.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Is peer
summary: A yes/no check on the capital's owner about being a peer of the player; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name only. What the game counts as a peer is not documented here. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Is raiding me
summary: A yes/no check whether the capital's owner is raiding the player, going by its name.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Is realm capital
summary: Whether the icon marks the capital of a whole realm.
details: Going by its name only; vanilla uses a function of the same name on provinces and other icons, not on this type.

label: Is top liege
summary: A yes/no check on the capital's owner about being a top liege; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Is vassal
summary: A yes/no check on the capital's owner about a vassal relation to the player; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name only. Whether it means the owner is the player's vassal is a guess. Vanilla never uses it.

label: On holding clicked
summary: Reacts to a click on the holding of a capital map icon; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name only. It returns nothing. Vanilla never uses it.

label: This capital icon
summary: A game function of a capital icon on the map that stands for the icon itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla does not use it with this type. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: Access this candidate
summary: A game function of a cardinal candidate entry that hands back the entry itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Its return type is listed as unregistered, and vanilla never uses it with this type.

label: Archetype description
summary: The description text of the candidate's archetype.
details: Vanilla uses it in the candidate tooltip of the cardinals window, right after the archetype's name and before the line saying which rite the character follows. The game does not say what an archetype is.

label: Archetype name
summary: The name of the candidate's archetype.
details: Vanilla uses it as the heading of the candidate tooltip, in a debug text of the cardinals window, and as the `text` of a label in the cardinals window.

label: The cardinal
summary: The cardinal (a character) that this candidate entry stands for.
details: Vanilla sets it as the `datacontext` of widgets in the cardinals window, so they can show that character's data. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: Candidate key
summary: The key of the candidate entry, as text.
details: Vanilla compares it with the texts `theocratic_elective_populist`, `theocratic_elective_powerful` and `theocratic_elective_pious` in the cardinals window to show different things per kind of candidate, and with the key of a voter list's owner to dim lists of other candidates.

label: Preferred tenet
summary: The tenet (a core belief of a faith) that this candidate prefers.
details: Vanilla uses it as a `datacontext` in the cardinals window and in the text that says the elected candidate will replace one tenet with their preferred one. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: Score breakdown
summary: A text that lists how the candidate's score is made up.
details: Vanilla uses it in the candidate tooltip and in a debug text of the cardinals window.

label: Supporter count
summary: How many supporters the candidate has, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it as the `text` of a label in the cardinals window.

label: Swapped out tenet
summary: The tenet that the candidate would replace if elected.
details: Vanilla uses it as a `datacontext` in the cardinals window and in the text 'will replace [this tenet] with [their] preferred tenet'. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: This candidate
summary: The candidate entry itself, used as an argument for other functions.
details: Vanilla passes it to `CardinalsWindow.OnClickCardinalCandidate` when a candidate is clicked. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: Will swap tenets
summary: Whether electing this candidate would swap a tenet of the faith.
details: Vanilla uses it in `visible` lines of the cardinals window, also combined with a check that the character is not the local player.

label: Access this cardinal entry
summary: A game function of a cardinal entry that hands back the entry itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Its return type is listed as unregistered, and vanilla never uses it with this type.

label: The cardinal
summary: The character that this cardinal entry stands for.
details: Vanilla sets it as the `datacontext` of widgets in the cardinals window, so they can show that character's data. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: Pope chance
summary: The predicted chance that this cardinal becomes the next Pope, as a number.
details: Vanilla writes it as a percentage in the text 'Likelihood of being the next Pope'.

label: Vote for
summary: Whom this cardinal votes for; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: This cardinal entry
summary: A game function of a cardinal entry that stands for the entry itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla does not use it with this type. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: Access this voter list
summary: A game function of the list of voting characters that hands back the list itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Its return type is listed as unregistered, and vanilla never uses it with this type.

label: Elector of a character
summary: The elector entry that belongs to a given character.
details: Vanilla passes `Character.Self` and uses the result as a `datacontext` in the cardinals window. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character whose elector entry is wanted.

label: List owner
summary: The candidate that this list of voters belongs to.
details: Vanilla compares it with `CardinalCandidateItem.Self` using `ObjectsEqual`, and reads its key (`GetKey`) to tell candidate kinds apart. Going by those uses, the owner is a candidate entry. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: This voter list
summary: A game function of the list of voting characters that stands for the list itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla does not use it with this type. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: Access this window
summary: A game function of the cardinals window that hands back the window itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Its return type is listed as unregistered, and vanilla never uses it with this window.

label: Close window
summary: Closes the cardinals window.
details: Vanilla runs it from an `onclick` line of the cardinals window. It returns nothing.

label: Cardinal candidates
summary: The list of candidates shown in the cardinals window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the `datamodel` of lists in the cardinals window, so each candidate becomes one entry. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: Cardinal electors
summary: The list of electors (the cardinals who vote); the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: Voter characters
summary: The voting characters of the cardinals window, handed on as data for a widget.
details: Vanilla sets it as the `datacontext` of a widget in the cardinals window. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: Voter list
summary: The list of voters of the cardinals window, handed on as data for a widget.
details: Vanilla sets it as the `datacontext` of widgets in the cardinals window. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: Faith of the window
summary: The faith that the cardinals window is about, going by its name.
details: Going by its name and its use, vanilla sets it as the `datacontext` of a widget in the cardinals window. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: Is active tab
summary: Whether the tab with the given name is the one currently open in the cardinals window.
details: Vanilla asks it for the tabs `bookmark_college` and `bookmark_succession`, and uses the answer to clear a stored variable when that tab is not open.

label: Click on candidate
summary: Reacts to a click on a cardinal candidate.
details: Vanilla runs it from an `onclick` line and passes `CardinalCandidateItem.Self`, the clicked candidate. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a candidate entry, such as CardinalCandidateItem.Self

label: This window
summary: A game function of the cardinals window that stands for the window itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla does not use it with this window. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: Set active tab
summary: Opens the tab with the given name in the cardinals window; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it with this window; the faith window has a function of the same name, `FaithWindow.SetActiveTab`, that is run on start and on click. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the tab to open.
fields.values: a text such as a tab name

label: Access this casus belli entry
summary: A game function of a casus belli entry that hands back the entry itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Its return type is listed as unregistered, and vanilla never uses it with this type.

label: Character
summary: A character belonging to the casus belli entry; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it with this type. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: Invalid reason text
summary: The text that, going by its name, says why the casus belli entry is invalid.
details: Vanilla puts it in the `tooltip` line of the declare-war window.

label: War reason label
summary: The label of a casus belli (a reason for war), as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as the `text` in the declare-war window.

label: Casus belli type
summary: The casus belli type of the entry.
details: Vanilla reads the type's icon with `.GetIcon` for the `texture` of an image in the declare-war window. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: Is selected
summary: Whether this casus belli is the selected one in the declare-war window.
details: Vanilla uses it in `visible` and `down` (pressed look) lines of the declare-war window.

label: Is valid
summary: Whether the casus belli entry is valid.
details: Vanilla negates it with `Not` in a `visible` line of the declare-war window, so something is shown when the entry is not valid. The entry's `GetInvalidText` is used as a tooltip in the same window. The game does not say what makes an entry valid.

label: On click
summary: Reacts to a click on a casus belli entry.
details: Vanilla runs it from `onclick` lines of the declare-war window. Going by the selected check, it selects that casus belli. It returns nothing.

label: This casus belli entry
summary: A game function of a casus belli entry that stands for the entry itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla does not use it with this type. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: Access this title entry
summary: A game function of a title entry in the declare-war window that hands back the entry itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Its return type is listed as unregistered, and vanilla never uses it with this type.

label: Blockers text
summary: The blocker text of a title entry; going by its name, what stands in the way of the claim on that title.
details: Vanilla puts it in front of the click hints 'Click to toggle the claim for ...' and 'Click to select the claim for ...' in the tooltips of the declare-war window.

label: Title name
summary: The name of the title of this entry, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as the `text` in the declare-war window, with the `|U` format that makes the first letter upper case.

label: Size
summary: The size of the entry as a vector of two numbers; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name and its return type only. Vanilla uses `InteractionTitleItem.GetSize` for a `size` line, which is a different type.

label: The title
summary: The title that this entry stands for.
details: Vanilla sets it as a `datacontext` in the declare-war window and reads its name with `.GetName` in click hints. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: Is enabled
summary: Whether the title entry can be used; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it with this type; other types have an `IsEnabled` too (for example `Dlc.IsEnabled` in a `visible` line), but that is only a hint.

label: Is selected
summary: Whether this title entry is the selected one.
details: Vanilla uses it in a `down` line (pressed look) of the declare-war window.

label: On click
summary: Reacts to a click on a title entry in the declare-war window.
details: Vanilla runs it from an `onclick` line. Going by the click hints, it toggles or selects the claim on that title. It returns nothing.

label: This title entry
summary: A game function of a title entry in the declare-war window that stands for the entry itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla does not use it with this type. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: Access this casus belli type
summary: A game function of a casus belli type that hands back the type itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Its return type is listed as unregistered, and vanilla never uses it with this type.

label: Custom text
summary: A custom text of the casus belli type, chosen by name; the game documents nothing more.
details: Returns text. Vanilla does not use it with this type. Other types use a function `Custom` with a text name to call a named custom text, but that is only a hint here.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the custom text.

label: Icon
summary: The icon of the casus belli type.
details: Vanilla reads it in the declare-war window as `CasusBelliItem.GetType.GetIcon` for an image `texture`. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: Name
summary: The name of the casus belli type, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as the `text` in a debug window that watches the AI.

label: Attacker faith might join
summary: Whether the attacker's faith might join the war when this casus belli is used.
details: Vanilla uses it through `DeclareWarInteractionWindow.GetCbType` in a `visible` line of the declare-war window. The reading rests on the name and that use.

label: Defender faith might join
summary: Whether the defender's faith might join the war when this casus belli is used.
details: Vanilla uses it through `DeclareWarInteractionWindow.GetCbType` in a `visible` line of the declare-war window. The reading rests on the name and that use.

label: Has icon
summary: Whether the casus belli type has an icon; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla uses `HasIcon` on other types (concept tooltips, laws, situation phases) in `visible` lines. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: Is white peace possible
summary: Whether a war with this casus belli can end in a white peace (no winner).
details: Vanilla uses it in `visible` lines of the declare-war window and of the war overview window, the latter through the active casus belli of the war. The reading rests on the name and those uses.

label: This casus belli type
summary: A game function of a casus belli type that stands for the type itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla does not use it with this type. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: Access this catalyst entry
summary: A game function of a catalyst entry that hands back the entry itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Its return type is listed as unregistered, and vanilla never uses it with this type.

label: The catalyst
summary: The catalyst that this entry stands for.
details: Vanilla passes it to `Struggle.GetNumCompletionsOfCatalystForPhase` in the struggle window, to count how often this catalyst happened in the selected phase. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: Catalyst description
summary: The description text of the catalyst.
details: Vanilla uses it as the whole text of the phase catalyst entry line in the struggle texts.

label: Catalyst worth
summary: How much the catalyst is worth, as a whole number; going by its name, its effect on the struggle's progress.
details: Vanilla shows it with the `|+=` format in the struggle window, which colours and signs the number as a gain or loss. It can be negative going by that format.

label: This catalyst entry
summary: A game function of a catalyst entry that stands for the entry itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla does not use it with this type. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: Access this history entry
summary: A game function of a catalyst history entry that hands back the entry itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Its return type is listed as unregistered, and vanilla never uses it with this type.

label: Triggering character
summary: The character that triggered this catalyst entry in the struggle's history.
details: Vanilla shows its name in the struggle tooltips, and asks `IsValid` on it to choose between a text with a character and one without. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: Date
summary: The date when this catalyst entry happened.
details: Vanilla writes it in the struggle tooltips with `.GetString` or `.GetStringLong`. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: Progress
summary: The progress value of this catalyst entry, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla writes it with the `|+=` format at the start of the struggle tooltips, which signs and colours the number, so it can be negative. The game does not say more.

label: Struggle phase
summary: The struggle phase that this catalyst entry belongs to.
details: Vanilla compares it with `Struggle.GetCurrentLeadingPhase` using `ObjectsEqual` in `visible` lines of the shared tooltip, to tell whether the entry belongs to the phase now leading. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: This history entry
summary: A game function of a catalyst history entry that stands for the entry itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla does not use it with this type. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: Access this sub-window
summary: A game function of the catalyst sub-window that hands back the sub-window itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Its return type is listed as unregistered, and vanilla never uses it with this type.

label: Close sub-window
summary: Closes the catalyst sub-window.
details: Vanilla runs it from an `onclick` line of the Christian church window. It returns nothing.

label: Catalyst items
summary: The list of catalysts shown in the sub-window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the `datamodel` of a list in the Christian church window. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: Shown phase type
summary: The situation phase type the sub-window is set to, going by its name.
details: Vanilla compares it with `SituationPhaseType.Self` to light up the matching button, reads its icon, and uses it as a `datacontext`. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: Future situation phase
summary: A future phase of the situation, handed on as data for a widget.
details: Going by its name and its use as a `datacontext` in the Christian church window. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: Situation sub-region
summary: The sub-region of the situation that the sub-window was set up with.
details: Vanilla reads `.GetCurrentPhase` from it and uses that as a `datacontext` in the Christian church window. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: Is visible
summary: Whether the catalyst sub-window is shown, going by its name.
details: Vanilla uses it in the Christian church window, combined with `And`: in a `down` line (pressed look) of a phase button together with a check that the phase type matches, and in a `visible` line.

label: This sub-window
summary: A game function of the catalyst sub-window that stands for the sub-window itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla does not use it with this type. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: Set situation data
summary: Gives the sub-window the sub-region and the phase type to show catalysts for.
details: Vanilla runs it from an `onclick` line with `Situation.GetTopSubRegion.Self` and `SituationPhaseType.Self`. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a situation sub-region, as in vanilla `Situation.GetTopSubRegion.Self`

fields.name: Arg1
fields.values: a phase type, such as SituationPhaseType.Self

label: Show sub-window
summary: Shows the catalyst sub-window; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it with this type. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle sub-window
summary: Switches the catalyst sub-window between shown and hidden; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it with this type; the lines found with the same name are texts of other things. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle if same
summary: Toggles the sub-window when the given phase type is the one already shown.
details: Vanilla runs it from an `onclick` line with `SituationPhaseType.Self`. The reading rests on its name and that use. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The phase type to compare with the one shown.
fields.values: a phase type, such as SituationPhaseType.Self

label: Access this catalyst type
summary: A game function of a catalyst type that hands back the type itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Its return type is listed as unregistered, and vanilla never uses it with this type.

label: This catalyst type
summary: A game function of a catalyst type that stands for the type itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla does not use it with this type. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: Access this challenge character
summary: A game function of a challenge character (a start choice in the main menu) that hands back the entry itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Its return type is listed as unregistered, and vanilla never uses it with this type.

label: Age
summary: The age of the challenge character, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it after the name in the info text of a challenge character. The game does not state the unit.

label: Bookmark character
summary: The bookmark character that belongs to this challenge character.
details: Returns a bookmark character. Vanilla sets it as a `datacontext` in the main menu so its widgets can show that character.

label: Start date
summary: The date at which this challenge character starts.
details: Returns a date. Vanilla writes it in the main menu with `.GetStringLong`.

label: This challenge character
summary: A game function of a challenge character that stands for the entry itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla does not use it with this type. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: Access this challenger
summary: A game function of a challenger entry that hands back the entry itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Its return type is listed as unregistered, and vanilla never uses it with this type.

label: Challenger title
summary: The title of the challenger, going by its name.
details: Vanilla uses it as a `datacontext` in the faith window, and reads the holder of the title with `.GetHolder` to get the challenger as a character. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: Sponsor title
summary: The title held by the challenger's sponsor.
details: Vanilla compares it with the challenger's title using `ObjectsEqual` in `visible` lines of the faith window, and uses it as a `datacontext`. Its return type is listed as unregistered. The word 'sponsor' is taken from the name.

label: This challenger
summary: A game function of a challenger entry that stands for the entry itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla does not use it with this type. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: Access this window
summary: A game function of the challengers window that hands back the window itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Its return type is listed as unregistered, and vanilla never uses it with this window.

label: Close window
summary: Closes the challengers window.
details: Vanilla runs it from an `onclick` line and from an `on_start` line of the faith window. It returns nothing.

label: Challenger of a character
summary: The challenger entry that belongs to a given character.
details: Vanilla passes `Character.Self` and uses the result as a `datacontext` in the faith window. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character whose challenger entry is wanted.

label: Challengers list
summary: The list of challengers of the challengers window, handed on as data for a widget.
details: Vanilla sets it as the `datacontext` of a widget in the faith window. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: Is visible
summary: Whether the challengers window is open.
details: Vanilla uses it in `visible` and `down` (pressed look) lines of the faith window.

label: This window
summary: A game function of the challengers window that stands for the window itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla does not use it with this window. Its return type is listed as unregistered.

label: Toggle window
summary: Opens the challengers window if it is closed, or closes it if it is open.
details: Vanilla runs it from an `onclick` line of the faith window. The reading rests on its name and that use. It returns nothing.
